notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Some Tennessee cities run their own school systems; where this one does, school spending is included and left out of the services and overhead shares. Residents also pay Lawrence County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
The city borrowed $2,865,000 during the year, which is not counted as revenue but helps explain spending above revenue.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Tennessee city candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 8 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Lawrenceburg's borders in OpenStreetMap (8 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Tennessee yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 8 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Lawrenceburg's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

source.label: OpenStreetMap license-plate cameras (as mapped by DeFlock)

redFlags.label: Third-party investigative platform
redFlags.detail: The Lawrenceburg Police Department has access to SoundThinking's CrimeTracer (formerly Coplink X) investigative platform through a statewide contract announced in April 2021.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012478, citing PR News Wire

redFlags.unscoredReason: Not scored: every police department in the state has this through a statewide contract, so it is not a local decision.
